subject.title: Gateway crash-loops with default Node heap (~4 GB) — make 'openclaw daemon install' set NODE_OPTIONS or accept a --heap-mb flag

question: Should OpenClaw resolve this issue by accepting the fixed 8192 MB managed-service heap default in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/96250, requiring a tunable CLI/config surface first, or rejecting daemon heap changes for now?
rationale: The code path is clear, but the fix changes generated service startup defaults and intersects the blocked `NODE_OPTIONS` boundary, low-memory-host behavior, and reinstall semantics, so maintainer product and compatibility intent is required.

options.title: Accept Fixed Default
options.body: Land the narrow fixed-default mitigation if maintainers accept the 8192 MB cap as the emergency daemon-install behavior and track durable tuning separately.

options.title: Require Tunable Surface
options.body: Pause the fix until maintainers choose a CLI/config/doctor surface and upgrade behavior for host-specific heap sizing.

options.title: Reject Daemon Heap Change
options.body: Keep current daemon service defaults and rely on manual wrapper/service edits or state cleanup instead of changing OpenClaw-generated startup behavior.

recommendation.title: Accept Fixed Default
recommendation.body: Land the narrow fixed-default mitigation if maintainers accept the 8192 MB cap as the emergency daemon-install behavior and track durable tuning separately.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent and historical signal across daemon service environment, wrapper persistence, and install-helper behavior that frames this product tradeoff.
